result.headline: Actuator output ch[4] froze at 1500 us from t=49.7 s while its twin ch[5] kept moving.
result.explanation: Output channel 4 stopped following its mirror channel 5 at about 49.7 s. Whether the cause is mixer/output software, the driver or the servo cannot be separated from this recording.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[4]] held 1500 from t=49.711 to 81.163 s (94 samples)
evidence.shows: ch[4] stuck at neutral to the end of the recording (94 samples). Neutral is plausible as a failsafe or hold value.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[4]] at t=1.901 s: 1550 -> 1439.5 us (step -110.5, 36.8x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: ch[4] moved with ch[5] earlier (same step at 1.901 s on both, lines 39 and 42). Both channels were identical for t=0 to 49.4 s (correlation 1.0, difference 0), then diverged after the freeze (typical difference 20 us, worst 119 us at t=78.099 s).

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[5]] at t=77.048 s: 1510.5 -> 1386.5 us (step -124, 15.5x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: ch[5] kept responding to the controller after ch[4] froze, so the controller was still commanding and the output path was not dead.
Roll error rises after the freeze (10.922, 6.953, 7.201 deg against 1.831 deg just before). The first 8 s were just as bad (10.96) with no freeze, so this is only a weak link.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.273 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: Sensor health error and low-voltage warning at t=0.273 s, both in the first sample. They predate the freeze by about 49 s, and no later events were recorded.

checked.check: Did any signal leave baseline before the early events (0-8 s)?
checked.result: No signal left baseline ahead of the two start-of-recording events at 0.273 s.

checked.check: Relation of ch[4] to its twin ch[5] before the freeze (t=0 to 49.5 s)
Relation of ch[4] to ch[5] after the freeze (t=49.8 to 81.3 s)
checked.result: Correlation is undefined because ch[4] is constant. Typical difference 20 us, worst 119 us at t=78.099 s. ch[5] spans 1381-1565 us.

checked.check: Which signals left baseline first around 49-58 s
checked.result: Only the setpoints (yaw at 57.215 s, roll at 57.966 s) moved. No event fired and the attitude did not move first.

checked.check: Roll and pitch setpoint tracking over the whole run
checked.result: Roll correlation 0.839, rising to 0.983 at a 0.974 s lag. Pitch correlation -0.487, reaching -0.896 at a 1.461 s lag.

effects.why: Roll tracking worsens after ch[4] stops following. This may be an effect, but the 0-8 s stretch was as bad.

effects.quote: EVENT t=0.273 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
effects.why: First-sample event. It cannot be the consequence of a freeze at 49.7 s and is not shown to be its cause.

next_action.action: Bench-test ch[4] and ch[5] with a roll command, propellers off.
next_action.why: Separates a software or mixer output hold from a driver or servo fault on ch[4], which the recording cannot show.
how: Power the airframe on the bench with the propeller removed and the power system safe.
Command roll in a stabilised mode and log actuator.output ch[4] and ch[5] and the mixer/output-group config.
Watch the physical surface or servo on ch[4] against its logged output.
Compare the mixer mapping and any failsafe or neutral-hold setting for ch[4].
next_action.conditions: Bench, props off, same firmware and mixer config as flight 30. Command roll in steps as the flight did, with battery voltage normal.
next_action.baseline: ch[5] response and the t=0-49 s behaviour of ch[4], where both channels were identical.

outcomes.label: ch[4] logged output stays at 1500
outcomes.means: The output is held at neutral in software or config. The cause is in the mixer, output group or failsafe logic, not the servo.
outcomes.then: Inspect firmware mixer and output-hold conditions around 49.7 s.

outcomes.label: Logged ch[4] moves and the servo follows
outcomes.means: The freeze does not reproduce on the bench. It may need flight conditions such as the low-voltage state or vibration.
outcomes.then: Request raw flight data and compare the bench run with the flight.

outcomes.label: Logged ch[4] moves but the servo does not
outcomes.means: Driver or servo fault on ch[4]. The recorded output was normal, so the in-flight record would not show it.
outcomes.then: Inspect the servo, wiring and connector on ch[4].

unknowns: Whether the ch[4] servo physically stopped, since the recording holds only the commanded output.
What triggered the freeze at about 49.7 s: no event or signal departure was recorded just before it.
Whether the roll error after 57 s comes from the freeze or from the flight manoeuvres.

hypotheses.claim: The output for ch[4] was held at neutral by firmware or output logic from t=49.7 s while ch[5] kept running.
hypotheses.because: Twin channels were identical until 49.4 s, then ch[4] froze while ch[5] continued. This was observed at the commanded outputs.

hypotheses.claim: The mixer or channel mapping for ch[4] changed or dropped out, for example through a failsafe neutral-hold.
hypotheses.because: The freeze value 1500 is the neutral value, but no failsafe event was recorded around 49.7 s.

hypotheses.claim: Driver, servo or wiring on ch[4] fails, with the output log reflecting an output-stage hold.
hypotheses.because: A hardware fault cannot be seen in commanded outputs, so it is not excluded. The recording does not observe the servo.

hypotheses.claim: Bad attitude estimate or sensor health caused the roll and pitch divergence rather than an output fault.
hypotheses.because: Roll follows the setpoint at 0.983 correlation with a 0.974 s lag, so much of the tracking error is lag. The sensor-health error at 0.273 s remains unexplained.

hypotheses.claim: Low supply voltage affected outputs or the controller.
